From 1799d8abeabc68ec05679292aaf6cba93b343c05 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Jiayuan Chen <jiayuan.chen@shopee.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Jan 2026 19:38:44 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] xfrm6: fix uninitialized saddr in xfrm6_get_saddr()

xfrm6_get_saddr() does not check the return value of
ipv6_dev_get_saddr(). When ipv6_dev_get_saddr() fails to find a suitable
source address (returns -EADDRNOTAVAIL), saddr->in6 is left
uninitialized, but xfrm6_get_saddr() still returns 0 (success).

This causes the caller xfrm_tmpl_resolve_one() to use the uninitialized
address in xfrm_state_find(), triggering KMSAN warning:

=====================================================
BUG: KMSAN: uninit-value in xfrm_state_find+0x2424/0xa940
 xfrm_state_find+0x2424/0xa940
 xfrm_resolve_and_create_bundle+0x906/0x5a20
 xfrm_lookup_with_ifid+0xcc0/0x3770
 xfrm_lookup_route+0x63/0x2b0
 ip_route_output_flow+0x1ce/0x270
 udp_sendmsg+0x2ce1/0x3400
 inet_sendmsg+0x1ef/0x2a0
 __sock_sendmsg+0x278/0x3d0
 __sys_sendto+0x593/0x720
 __x64_sys_sendto+0x130/0x200
 x64_sys_call+0x332b/0x3e70
 do_syscall_64+0xd3/0xf80
 entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe+0x77/0x7f

Local variable tmp.i.i created at:
 xfrm_resolve_and_create_bundle+0x3e3/0x5a20
 xfrm_lookup_with_ifid+0xcc0/0x3770
=====================================================

Fix by checking the return value of ipv6_dev_get_saddr() and propagating
the error.

Fixes: a1e59abf8249 ("[XFRM]: Fix wildcard as tunnel source")
Reported-by: syzbot+e136d86d34b42399a8b1@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Closes: https://lore.kernel.org/all/68bf1024.a70a0220.7a912.02c2.GAE@google.com/T/
Signed-off-by: Jiayuan Chen <jiayuan.chen@shopee.com>
Signed-off-by: Jiayuan Chen <jiayuan.chen@linux.dev>
Reviewed-by: Simon Horman <horms@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Steffen Klassert <steffen.klassert@secunet.com>

diff --git a/net/ipv6/xfrm6_policy.c b/net/ipv6/xfrm6_policy.c
index 1f19b6f14484..125ea9a5b8a0 100644
--- a/net/ipv6/xfrm6_policy.c
+++ b/net/ipv6/xfrm6_policy.c
@@ -57,6 +57,7 @@ static int xfrm6_get_saddr(xfrm_address_t *saddr,
 	struct dst_entry *dst;
 	struct net_device *dev;
 	struct inet6_dev *idev;
+	int err;
 
 	dst = xfrm6_dst_lookup(params);
 	if (IS_ERR(dst))
@@ -68,9 +69,11 @@ static int xfrm6_get_saddr(xfrm_address_t *saddr,
 		return -EHOSTUNREACH;
 	}
 	dev = idev->dev;
-	ipv6_dev_get_saddr(dev_net(dev), dev, &params->daddr->in6, 0,
-			   &saddr->in6);
+	err = ipv6_dev_get_saddr(dev_net(dev), dev, &params->daddr->in6, 0,
+				 &saddr->in6);
 	dst_release(dst);
+	if (err)
+		return -EHOSTUNREACH;
 	return 0;
 }
 
-- 
2.34.1

The patch fixes an uninitialized source address bug in `xfrm6_get_saddr()` by checking the return value of `ipv6_dev_get_saddr()` and propagating errors.

## Modifications in each file

- **`net/ipv6/xfrm6_policy.c`**:
  - Added an `int err` variable to capture the return value of `ipv6_dev_get_saddr()`.
  - Changed the call from `ipv6_dev_get_saddr(...)` (without error check) to `err = ipv6_dev_get_saddr(...)`.
  - Added a check: if `err` is non-zero, return `-EHOSTUNREACH` after releasing the dst reference; otherwise, return 0.

## Relationships between modifications

The change is isolated to a single function (`xfrm6_get_saddr`) within one file. The key relationship is that the previously missing error check leads to an uninitialized `saddr->in6` being used by callers (e.g., `xfrm_state_find()` via `xfrm_tmpl_resolve_one()`), causing KMSAN warnings. By capturing and propagating the error from `ipv6_dev_get_saddr()`, the patch prevents the use of uninitialized data and aligns the function’s behavior with its documented contract (returning 0 on success, negative on failure). No other files are affected.

Here is the root cause:
Missing error check for the return value of ipv6_dev_get_saddr() in xfrm6_get_saddr(), allowing an uninitialized source address to be used when the function fails.

Here is the patch:
 
 static int xfrm6_get_saddr(xfrm_address_t *saddr,
 			   const struct xfrm_dst_lookup_params *params)
 {
 	struct dst_entry *dst;
 	struct net_device *dev;
 	struct inet6_dev *idev;
+	int err;
 
 	dst = xfrm6_dst_lookup(params);
 	if (IS_ERR(dst))
 		return -EHOSTUNREACH;
 
 	idev = ip6_dst_idev(dst);
 	if (!idev) {
 		dst_release(dst);
 		return -EHOSTUNREACH;
 	}
 	dev = idev->dev;
-	ipv6_dev_get_saddr(dev_net(dev), dev, &params->daddr->in6, 0,
-			   &saddr->in6);
+	err = ipv6_dev_get_saddr(dev_net(dev), dev, &params->daddr->in6, 0,
+				 &saddr->in6);
 	dst_release(dst);
+	if (err)
+		return -EHOSTUNREACH;
 	return 0;
 }

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
`ipv6_dev_get_saddr(dev_net(dev), dev, &params->daddr->in6, 0, &saddr->in6);`
`return 0;`
Reason:
The return value of `ipv6_dev_get_saddr()` is not checked. When it fails (e.g., returns -EADDRNOTAVAIL because no suitable source address exists), `saddr->in6` remains uninitialized, but the function still returns 0 (success). This causes the caller to use the uninitialized address, leading to KMSAN warnings and potential undefined behavior.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
`err = ipv6_dev_get_saddr(dev_net(dev), dev, &params->daddr->in6, 0, &saddr->in6);`
`if (err)`
`	return -EHOSTUNREACH;`
Reason:
By storing the return value of `ipv6_dev_get_saddr()` in `err` and checking it, the function now propagates the error when `ipv6_dev_get_saddr()` fails. Returning `-EHOSTUNREACH` prevents the caller from using an uninitialized `saddr`, eliminating the uninitialized memory access and the associated KMSAN warning.
